description: Postgres efficiency: the most expensive queries across beads, litellm and keycloak (pg_stat_statements), table sizes and write rates, dead tuples and autovacuum, connections by state and application, postgres CPU against its node, and kbeads latency on the same axis. Open this when postgres is slow or busy.

options.content: Postgres efficiency, from the `postgres_exporter` sidecar in the postgres pod (gd-cawNAc0iU7). **Top queries** come from `pg_stat_statements` across every database (beads, litellm, keycloak): the 50 with the most total execution time, normalized text cut to 120 characters, string literals shown as `?`. **Tables** are, per database, the 20 largest by total size (incl. TOAST and indexes) plus the 10 with the most rows written. **CPU** is read by postgres itself (container cgroup and node `/proc/stat`), since k3s scrapes no cAdvisor series. Counters reset when pg_stat_statements evicts or resets, and a query that leaves the top 50 stops reporting, so rates are the reliable view. Owner direction: make the queries cheaper, not the box bigger.

panels.title: Exporter up
panels.description: pg_up from the sidecar: 0 means the exporter cannot reach postgres (or the exporter-setup container has not created its role yet).

panels.title: Postgres CPU
panels.description: CPU cores the postgres container used (cgroup cpu.stat usage_usec), 5m rate.

panels.title: Node CPU busy
panels.description: Share of the postgres node's CPU that is not idle or iowait (/proc/stat), 5m rate.

panels.title: Longest active query
panels.description: Age of the oldest query in state=active, any database. The 0 fallback is gated on pg_up==1, so with the exporter down or postgres unreachable the panel shows no data instead of a false 0.

panels.title: Oldest open transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction (incl. idle in transaction). Old ones hold back vacuum. The 0 fallback is gated on pg_up==1, so with the exporter down or postgres unreachable the panel shows no data instead of a false 0.

panels.title: Total database size
panels.description: Sum of pg_database_size over all databases.

panels.title: Top queries over the time range
panels.description: The 15 statements with the most execution time in the selected range. Mean = time / calls in the range; hit ratio = shared buffer hits / (hits + reads).

targets.expr: sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_calls{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) and on (datname, queryid) topk(15, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])))

(sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) / (sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_calls{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) > 0)) and on (datname, queryid) topk(15, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])))

(sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_rows{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) / (sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_calls{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) > 0)) and on (datname, queryid) topk(15, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])))

(sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_shared_blks_hit{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) / (sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_shared_blks_hit{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range]) + increase(pg_top_statements_shared_blks_read{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])) > 0)) and on (datname, queryid) topk(15, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (increase(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Top queries by total time
panels.description: DB seconds per second spent in each statement (1.0 = one core busy all the time). The best single view of what costs CPU.

panels.title: Top queries by mean time
panels.description: Mean execution time per call in the window, for statements called at least once in it. Dashed lines at 100 ms (orange) and 1 s (red) per call.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (rate(pg_top_statements_exec_seconds{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (datname, queryid, query) (rate(pg_top_statements_calls{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Calls per second
panels.description: Most frequently executed statements.

panels.title: Rows per call
panels.description: Rows returned or affected per call. A high value on a hot query usually means a missing LIMIT or filter.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (datname, queryid, query) (rate(pg_top_statements_rows{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (datname, queryid, query) (rate(pg_top_statements_calls{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Blocks read outside shared buffers
panels.description: Shared blocks each statement read from disk or the OS cache, as bytes/s (8 KiB blocks). Large values mean the working set does not fit in shared_buffers.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio per database
panels.description: blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read) from pg_stat_database. Below ~99% on an OLTP database is worth a look. Dashed lines at 90% (red below) and 99% (orange below); an OLTP database should sit above 99%.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per database.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: pg_database_size per database.

panels.title: Database growth per day
panels.description: Size slope over the last hour, scaled to a day. Sustained positive growth with flat row counts is bloat or history tables.

panels.title: Largest tables
panels.description: Total relation size (table + TOAST + indexes) of the 10 largest tables.

panels.title: Table growth per day
panels.description: Size slope of the fastest-growing tables over the last hour, scaled to a day.

panels.title: Inserts per table per hour
panels.description: Rows inserted in the last hour (n_tup_ins), top 10. A history table that grows with every write shows here first.

panels.title: Updates and deletes per table per hour
panels.description: Rows updated plus deleted in the last hour, top 10. Each one leaves a dead tuple for vacuum.

panels.title: Dead tuples
panels.description: Estimated dead rows waiting for vacuum, top 10 tables.

panels.title: Time since last autovacuum
panels.description: Seconds since autovacuum last processed the table; tables never autovacuumed are absent. Rising together with dead tuples means autovacuum is not keeping up. Dashed lines at 1 day (orange) and 1 week (red).

panels.title: Sequential vs index scans
panels.description: Scans per second on the tables with the most sequential scans. A big table with sequential scans and few index scans is missing an index.

targets.expr: sum by (datname, schemaname, relname) (rate(pg_top_tables_idx_scan{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (datname, schemaname, relname) topk(8, sum by (datname, schemaname, relname) (rate(pg_top_tables_seq_scan{component="postgres",datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Tables
panels.description: Per database: the 20 largest tables plus the 10 with the most rows written.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: Client backends by state, all databases.

panels.title: Connections by application
panels.description: Client backends by database and application_name ('unset' when the client sets none).

panels.title: Longest active query by application
panels.description: Age of the oldest active query per database and application. A sawtooth reaching the client timeout means queries are piling up. Dashed lines at 10 s and 60 s, as on the stat above.

panels.title: Oldest transaction by application
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction per database, application and state; idle in transaction holds locks and blocks vacuum. Dashed lines at 60 s and 10 min, as on the stat above.

panels.title: Active backends by wait type
panels.description: What active backends are waiting on: none = on CPU, Lock = blocked by another session, IO = reading.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: Locks held or awaited, by mode (pg_locks).

panels.title: Postgres CPU vs node CPU
panels.description: Cores used by the postgres container, cores busy on its node, and the node's core count, on one axis. Steal is CPU the hypervisor took (burstable instance credits).

panels.title: Postgres CPU throttling
panels.description: Seconds per second the postgres container spent CFS-throttled at its CPU limit. Any throttling means the CPU limit is too tight; dashed lines at 0.05 and 0.25.

panels.title: kbeads HTTP latency
panels.description: kbeads request duration p50 and p90 (gardenio_beads_http_request_duration_seconds), on the same time axis as the database panels. Dashed lines at 500 ms (orange) and 2 s (red).

panels.title: DB time per second vs kbeads requests
panels.description: Total DB seconds per second across the top statements, against kbeads requests per second.
